identity.name: People's Republic of Kampuchea
native_names: សាធារណរដ្ឋប្រជាមានិតកម្ពុជា (Sathéarônârôdth Brâchéaméanĭt Kâmpŭchéa)

land.text: Democratic Kampuchea, overthrown by the Vietnamese army and the KUFNS in early 1979

predecessors.note: Cliopatria's Khmer Rouge row (1976-1978) is the same outline of 184,307 km2. The Khmer Rouge kept the Thai-border jungle, so the handover is not total (see the ledger's contest).

land.text: the whole of Cambodia under the restored monarchy

successors.note: The PRK page: 'finally dissolved with the restoration of the Kingdom of Cambodia in September 1993' (the kingdom's own dossier gives 24 September). Cliopatria runs the PRK row to 1995 and starts the Kingdom row in 1996.

capitals.name: Phnom Penh
capitals.note: Infobox capital Phnom Penh; the PAVN and the KUFNS entered it on 7 January 1979.

keyframe_review.note: 184,307 km2 against the infobox's 181,035 km2 for 1980 (ratio 1.02); against {country: Cambodia} the shape has 13 cells outside and misses 14 of 623, i.e. a coarse outline. It draws all of Cambodia, while the pages say Vietnam's army 'controlled the major population centres' and the resistance held camps and outposts on the Thai border; neither page gives an extent, so the shape stands and the border strip is a ledger contest (confidence 2). It starts in 1979, the year of the PRK, and carries on through the State of Cambodia (renamed 30 April 1989).

correction.text: the same outline, held only until September 1993: the shape is unchanged and only its end year moves

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria keeps this shape to 1995, but the PRK page says the state 'was finally dissolved with the restoration of the Kingdom of Cambodia in September 1993' and Cliopatria's Kingdom of Cambodia row starts only in 1996; the kingdom dossier carries 1993-1995. Shape unchanged; it ends in 1993. UNTAC was established 28 February 1992 (infobox) and supervised the ceasefire and the 1993 election.

region.text: the KPRC 'proclaimed that the new official name of Cambodia was the People's Republic of Kampuchea'

ledger.note: 1979: the People's Republic of Kampuchea is proclaimed at Phnom Penh. Infobox 'Established as Kampuchean People's Revolutionary Council Government: 8 January 1979'; the renaming is dated '10 or 19 January 1979' in the infobox, so the page is inconsistent. 'On 7 January 1979, the PAVN entered Phnom Penh along with members of the KUFNS' (Cambodian-Vietnamese War page).

region.text: the Cambodian side of the Thai frontier, where the resistance 'operated from the refugee camps and from hidden military outposts along the Thai border'

ledger.note: 1979: the Khmer Rouge hold out on the Thai frontier. The Khmer Rouge 'was forced to retreat into the jungle near the border with Thailand'; Thailand sheltered them at Khao Larn camp (Trat); the KPNLF (Son Sann, October 1979) and FUNCINPEC fought too, and the CGDK coalition was formed on 22 June 1982. The retreat follows the fall of Phnom Penh (January 1979) but the page gives it no date and no extent, so the month is the fall of the capital and the strip is the two cells along the frontier (confidence 2).

region.text: Cambodia, whose 'major population centres' Vietnam's army controlled

ledger.note: 1979: Vietnamese occupation. Vietnam's army 'controlled the major population centres... from 1979 to September 1989'; the war page: the PRK's establishment on 8 January 1979 began 'a ten-year Vietnamese occupation'. The PRK is the Vietnamese-backed government on this land, hatched as occupation, not annexed.

1989: the PRK becomes the State of Cambodia. Infobox 30 April 1989; the body says the National Assembly acted on 29-30 April and the lead says the renaming began 'in May 1989', which the page does not reconcile. Same state and colour (rule 2).

September 1989: the Vietnamese army leaves. 'The remaining 26,000 left between 21 and 26 September 1989' (24,000 had left between April and July). The PRK page: the last troops 'were said to have left Cambodia on 26 September 1989', but 'probably did not leave until 1990'.

region.text: Pailin, attacked on 17 September 1989 and claimed by the Khmer Rouge on 24 October 1989

ledger.note: 24 October 1989: the Khmer Rouge take Pailin after the Vietnamese withdrawal. 'The Khmer Rouge attacked Pailin on 17 September 1989 and claimed the city on 24 October 1989.' The page does not say how long they held it nor the extent; the region is the Natural Earth province of Pailin (confidence 2). The kingdom dossier's 1993 gain covers the whole country, so Pailin appears there too.

region.text: the Cambodian side of the Thai frontier, where the resistance 'operated from the refugee camps and from hidden military outposts along the Thai border'

ledger.note: October 1991: the Paris Peace Agreements (23 October) open reconciliation and UNTAC (established 28 February 1992) supervises the ceasefire. The pages do not say the Khmer Rouge zone vanished: the contest ends on the treaty date and any later frontier fighting belongs to the Kingdom of Cambodia's dossier.

region.text: the whole of Cambodia under the restored monarchy

ledger.note: September 1993: the state ends with the restoration of the monarchy. 'Finally dissolved with the restoration of the Kingdom of Cambodia in September 1993' (the page gives no day; the kingdom dossier has 24 September). The infobox ends communist rule on 18 October 1991. The text names Heng Samrin head of state (the infobox's unlabelled list gives 1979-1992) and Hun Sen leader of the Council of Ministers from January 1985.

wars.name: Cambodian-Vietnamese War

zones.text: the Cambodian side of the Thai frontier, where the resistance 'operated from the refugee camps and from hidden military outposts along the Thai border'

wars.outcome: The Vietnamese army and the KUFNS overthrow Democratic Kampuchea in January 1979 and set up the PRK; the Khmer Rouge, the KPNLF and FUNCINPEC (the CGDK of 1982) fight from the Thai border until the Vietnamese withdrawal (21-26 September 1989) and the 1991 Paris Peace Accords.
wars.note: Infobox '23 December 1978 - 26 September 1989'. The K5 Plan (1984) tried to seal the Thai border and its first phase was completed in the 1984-85 dry-season offensive, when several resistance base camps were overrun; the page gives no map of control. The CGDK held the UN seat 'until 1993' (PRK page).

certainty.note: Control inside the frontier is approximate: the army held 'the major population centres' and the resistance the Thai-border camps and outposts, with no extent given by either page.
The 1991 Paris accords and UNTAC's ceasefire supervision; the page gives no frontier change.

sources.title: People's Republic of Kampuchea
sources.note: Identity, infobox area (181,035 km2, 1980), capital, 8 January 1979, the April 1989 renaming, occupation to September 1989, UNTAC, dissolution in September 1993.

sources.title: Cambodian-Vietnamese War
sources.note: The invasion, the fall of Phnom Penh on 7 January 1979, the Khmer Rouge retreat to the Thai border, the KPNLF and CGDK, the K5 Plan, the 1989 withdrawal and the Pailin attack of 1989.

notes: Written for batch se-04-c with two pages (the PRK article and the Cambodian-Vietnamese War article, the latter shared with the socialist-republic-of-vietnam dossier); the budget was 1-2. Cliopatria: the 1979 shape (to 1991) is all of Cambodia and is kept; the 1992 shape (to 1995) is trimmed to September 1993 because the PRK/State of Cambodia ends then and the kingdom's dossier (kingdom-of-cambodia_1993) covers 1993-1995. Cliopatria's own Khmer Rouge row ends in 1978, so the Khmer Rouge zone of 1979-1991 on the Thai border is not a Cliopatria shape at all. Page silent: the extent and any date of the Khmer Rouge/CGDK-held zones (so the strip along the Thai frontier is a confidence-2 reading), how long Pailin stayed in Khmer Rouge hands after 24 October 1989, the day of the 1993 dissolution (the kingdom dossier says 24 September 1993), the formation date of the CGDK (22 June 1982 is on the war page, not the PRK page, which says only 'in 1982'). The infobox heads of state (Heng Samrin 1979-1992 and others) are unlabelled, so no ruler strip is given. Counterparts needing dossiers (flagged in the report): the Coalition Government of Democratic Kampuchea and the Khmer Rouge's rump zones 1979-1993 (khmer-rouge only covers 1976-1978; suggested group se-04-x); the State of Cambodia is a rename here, not a separate state. The Vietnamese presence is recorded as occupation (the war page's word) paired with the occupation in the socialist-republic-of-vietnam dossier; a reviewer who prefers a client-state reading could convert both to vassal events. The Kingdom dossier records a 1993 gain from this state of the whole country, which includes the Pailin province this dossier loses in 1989.
